title: Readers accept plain format names and handler ids in the compiler, runtime, kb and workspace-runtime documents
summary: Every reader in these packages now accepts a document, receipt or wire format under a plain name with an integer `formatVersion` (1), such as `compiled-harness`, `position-packet`, `packet-receipt`, `kb-package`, `kb-selection`, `kb-citation`, `lifecycle-context` and `projection-catalog`, as well as under its original literal (`ia.<name>.v1`, `iakb.portable.v1`, `inventarch.method-bytes/1`). The prose projection profiles are also read as `claude-prose` and `codex-prose`, and `candidateValidation`, `managedPublication` and `Corpus` return an `adapters` map that answers the plain handler (`candidate-validate`, `draft-publish`, `corpus-inspect`) and the original one. Nothing written changes in this release: every writer still emits the original literal, profile id and handler id, so programs released earlier keep reading the output. A later release switches the writers to the plain names. `compileHarness` takes the `stamp` of a retained compilation so rebuilding it reproduces its digest. A format that is neither form is refused. The exported `KB_FORMAT` is now `kb-package`; `LEGACY_KB_FORMAT` holds the literal that packages still carry.
